title: Moxie Nerve Food created
phrase: the creation of Moxie Nerve Food
description: Augustin Thompson sold Moxie as a patent medicine against "paralysis, softening of the brain, nervousness, and insomnia." He claimed a Lieutenant Moxie found its secret plant, but the word likely comes from Maine's Abenaki or Algonquian place names. The secret plant was bitter gentian root, and Moxie is still Maine's official soft drink.

title: Dr Pepper first served
description: Pharmacist Charles Alderton created Dr Pepper at Morrison's Old Corner Drug Store in Waco, Texas, a year before Coca-Cola. And no, it doesn't contain prune juice.

title: Coca-Cola first sold
description: Five cents a glass at Jacob's Pharmacy in Atlanta. John Pemberton sold it as a temperance drink and a cure for morphine addiction, headaches, and more. The coca was cocaine, and the cola was caffeine from kola nuts.

title: Fig Newtons introduced
description: Named for Newton, Massachusetts, not Isaac. Nabisco dropped the "Fig" in 2012, partly because people associated figs with "olde" things.

title: Juicy Fruit gum introduced
phrase: the introduction of Juicy Fruit gum
description: William Wrigley Jr. started out selling soap with free baking powder, then baking powder with free gum. The gum won. Juicy Fruit is the oldest Wrigley flavor still made.

title: Pepsi created as Brad's Drink
description: Caleb Bradham first sold "Brad's Drink" at his drugstore in New Bern, North Carolina. He renamed it Pepsi-Cola in 1898 for its supposed digestive benefits.

title: Cracker Jack introduced
description: The Rueckheim brothers finally figured out how to keep the molasses popcorn from sticking together in clumps. One food historian calls it the first junk food.

title: Jell-O trademarked
description: Pearle and May Wait of Le Roy, New York, flavored gelatin with strawberry, raspberry, orange, and lemon. Pearle sold the rights two years later, and the buyer struggled to sell it.

title: Hershey bar first sold
description: Milton Hershey sold his caramel company to go all in on chocolate. The Hershey bar was the first mass-produced chocolate in the United States.

title: Barnum's Animals crackers introduced
phrase: the introduction of Barnum's Animals crackers
description: The box came with a string so you could hang it on the Christmas tree. It still does.

title: Triscuit introduced
description: "Baked by electricity" in Niagara Falls, next to the first major power plant in the United States. The name comes from electricity plus biscuit, as Triscuit's own Twitter account confirmed: "We had to go all the way up the ladder but we CAN confirm."

title: First Oreo sold
phrase: the first sale of an Oreo
description: Sold to a grocer in Hoboken, New Jersey, as an imitation of the Hydrox cookie. Oreos were made with lard until the 1990s.

title: Life Savers invented
description: Clarence Crane's chocolates melted in the summer, so he made a mint with a hole in it. His son was the poet Hart Crane.

title: Cheez-It crackers introduced
description: The Green & Green Company of Dayton, Ohio, sold them as a "baked rarebit." Six years later, H. P. Lovecraft's narrator in The Shadow over Innsmouth bought cheese crackers for his lunch.

title: Sliced bread first sold
phrase: the first sale of sliced bread
description: The Chillicothe Baking Company of Chillicothe, Missouri, sold the first loaves cut by Otto Rohwedder's slicing machine, advertising them as "the greatest forward step in the baking industry since bread was wrapped." By 1933 about 80% of the bread sold in the US came sliced. A wartime ban on sliced bread in 1943 lasted seven weeks.

title: Reese's Peanut Butter Cups created
phrase: the creation of Reese's Peanut Butter Cups
description: H. B. Reese managed a dairy barn for Milton Hershey until Hershey closed it to save money. So he started his own candy company, in Hershey, Pennsylvania, using Hershey's chocolate.

title: 7 Up launched
description: Sold for a while as "7up Lithiated Lemon Soda," with claims that it contained the mood stabilizer lithium citrate. The government made it drop the health claims, and it became plain 7 Up in 1937.

title: Twinkie invented
description: James Dewar noticed the strawberry shortcake machines sat idle out of season and used them for a snack cake with banana cream. Banana rationing in World War II switched it to vanilla.

title: Snickers introduced
description: Named after the Mars family's favorite horse.

title: Ritz Crackers introduced
description: In the middle of the Great Depression, Nabisco offered "a bite of the good life." The logo was inspired by the round label inside Sydney Stern's hat.

title: Spam introduced
description: Hormel's way to sell more pork shoulder. World War II and the occupations after it brought Spam to Guam, Hawaii, Okinawa, and the Philippines, where it became part of local cooking, like Spam musubi.

title: M&M's introduced
description: Forrest Mars got the idea from soldiers eating Smarties in the Spanish Civil War. The first big customer was the U.S. Army, and during World War II only the military could buy them.

title: Goldfish crackers invented
description: Oscar Kambly made them in Switzerland for his wife, a Pisces. Margaret Rudkin of Pepperidge Farm tried them on vacation and brought them to the US in 1962.

title: Pop-Tarts introduced
description: Post announced its toaster pastry months too early, and Kellogg's made its own in four months. The first shipment sold out in two weeks. The name is a pun on Pop Art.

title: Doritos go national
description: The first tortilla chip sold nationally in the US started at Casa de Fritos in Disneyland. The name comes from the Spanish doradito, "little golden thing."

title: Pringles introduced
description: The chip is a hyperbolic paraboloid. Science fiction author Gene Wolfe helped build the machine that cooks them, and part of the ashes of the can's inventor, Fredric Baur, were buried in one.
